I'm a PhD candidate in the Department of Econometrics and Business Statistics at Monash University.
I use mathematical models to understand how multidrug-resistant organisms spread through intensive care units.

My main project is a mechanistic transmission model of multidrug-resistant *Acinetobacter baumannii* in an ICU ward.
I fit it to hospital data, then use it to test infection control strategies such as environmental cleaning and patient screening.
I also study the risk factors behind hospital-acquired infections.

The models rely on ICU and microbiology records kept by hand in separate files.
To prepare them, I built a pipeline that links each patient's records by ID and name and notes how each match was made.

Behind every data point is a real person who was seriously unwell, and that keeps me grounded in this work.

Before the PhD, I spent two years as a research analyst at Sunway University's Institute for Global Strategy and Competitiveness, forecasting for national policy work and running data analytics workshops.
I also tutor statistics and analytics units at Monash in Malaysia and Australia.

My interests include computational epidemiology, infectious disease modeling, population health and health economics.
The part I enjoy most is inference: working out what the data says about how an infection moved through a ward, and how confident we can be in that answer.

Outside work: long walks 🚶‍♂️, the gym 🏋️, karaoke 🎤, gaming 🎮, the beach 🏖️, nature 🏔️, TV shows 📺, and resting.
